text: Why does everything keep getting more expensive?
One tiny island explains it.
On this island live ten people.
Every day, they catch ten fish.
And all the money on the island is one hundred seashells.
So one fish costs ten shells.
Simple.
Then one morning, the chief finds a hidden cave.
Full of shells.
Thousands of them.
He gives every islander a giant sack.
Everyone is rich!
They dance.
They cheer.
They run to the market.
But there's a problem.
The sea didn't change.
There are still only ten fish.
Now everyone can pay more.
So they do.
Twenty shells.
Fifty.
One hundred shells, for one fish.
By sunset, everyone is holding ten times the money,
and eating the exact same dinner.
But two people did not end up the same.
The chief spent his shells first, before prices rose.
He got a new boat.
And old Mara, who saved her shells in a jar for thirty years?
Her whole jar now buys a single fish.
Nobody got poorer by losing money.
They got poorer because someone made more of it.
That is inflation.
